groups.title: Section A · 第 1 篇 · 1–4 题
groups.material:
M: Today our guest is Rosie Mullender, who works as Features Editor for Fashion magazine. Hi, Rosie, you're Features Editor at one of the most widely-read women's magazines in the UK. What kind of responsibilities does that job entail?
W: We spend our days looking at ideas from journalists, writing copy for the magazine and website, and editing. We do random things like asking people in the street questions and testing sports clothing. We also do less tangible things like understanding what our readers want. It's certainly varied and sometimes bizarre.
M: During your working day, what kind of work might you typically do?
W: My day mainly incorporates responding to emails, writing and editing stories and coming up with new feature ideas.
M: How does the job of Features Editor differ from that of Fashion Editor, or other editorial positions?
W: The features team deals with articles such as careers, reports, confidence and confessions—everything except fashion and beauty.
M: A lot of people believe that working at a magazine is a glamorous job. Is this an accurate representation of what you do?
W: I'd say it's glamorous to an extent, but not in the way it's portrayed in films. We do have our moments, such as interviewing celebrities and attending parties, which is a huge thrill. Ultimately, though, we're the same as our readers, but working in a job we're all very lucky to have.
M: Did you have to overcome any difficulties to reach this point in your career? How did you manage to do this?
W: I had to be really persistent and it was very hard work. After three years of working in a petrol station and doing unpaid work, I still hadn't managed to get an entry-level job. I was lucky that my last desperate attempt led to a job. I told myself that all experiences make you a better journalist in the long run—and luckily, I was right!

groups.title: Section A · 第 2 篇 · 5–8 题
groups.material:
W: Are you watching any good shows these days?
M: Actually, yes. I'm watching a great satire called Frankie. I think you'd like it.
W: Really? What's it about?
M: It's about a real guy named Frankie. He is a famous comedian in New York and the show's a mixture of comedy and drama loosely depicting his life.
W: I'm sorry, do you mean to say, it's a real-life series about a real person? It's non-fiction, is it?
M: No… Not really, no. It's fiction, as what happens in every episode is made up. However the lead role is a comedian by the name of Frankie, and he plays himself. So Frankie in both real life and in the TV show lives in New York City, is a comic, is divorced, and has two little daughters. All those things are true, but aside from him, all his friends and family are played by actors. And the plots and events that take place are also invented.
W: Oh, I think I see now. That sounds like a very original concept.
M: Yes, it is. In fact, the whole show is written, directed, edited and produced by him, and is very funny and has won many awards.
W: That's cool. I will try to download it. I'm watching a comedy called The Big Bang Theory. It's a huge hit around the world.
M: Oh yes. I've heard of it, but never actually watched it.
W: Well, then you should check it out. It's also very funny. It's about four male scientists and a female waitress. The men are very socially awkward but very bright. And this is contrasted by the lady's social skills and common sense. The show has been running for over ten years, and some of the actors are practically global superstars, now that they are such famous celebrities.

groups.title: Section B · 第 1 篇 · 9–11 题
groups.material:
Related to the "use it or lose it" law is the "keep moving" principle.
We learned about stagnation from nature. A river that stops moving gets smelly. The same thing happens to people who stop moving, either mentally or physically. Those who play contact sports know that the player who usually gets hurt the most is the one who is standing still. Of course, you'll need some time to catch your breath every so often, but the essential message is "keep moving, extending and learning." Ships last a lot longer when they go to sea than when they stay in the harbor. The same is true for airplanes. You don't preserve an airplane by keeping it on the ground. You preserve it by keeping it in service.
We also get to live a long healthy life by staying in service. Longevity statistics reveal that the average person doesn't last very long after retirement. The moral here is don't retire. If a fellow says "I'm 94 years old and I worked all my life", we need to realize that is how he got to be 94, by staying involved. George Bernard Shaw won a Nobel Prize when he was nearly 70. Benjamin Franklin produced some of his best writings at the age of 84, and Pablo Picasso put brush to canvas right through his eighties. Isn't the issue how old we think we are?
A bonus with the "keep moving" principle is that while we keep moving, we don't have a chance to worry. Hence, we avoid the dreaded "paralysis by analysis".

groups.title: Section B · 第 2 篇 · 12–15 题
groups.material:
In 2014, one in 16 Americans visited the hospital emergency room for home injuries. One of the main causes of these accidents? A wandering mind. By one estimate, people daydream through nearly half of their waking hours.
Psychologists have recently focused on the tendency to think about something other than the task one is doing. For one experiment, researchers developed an app to analyze the relationship between daydreaming and happiness. They found that the average person's mind wandered most frequently (about 65% of the time) during personal activities, such as brushing their teeth and combing their hair. Respondents' minds tended to wander more when they felt upset rather than happy. They were more likely to wander toward pleasant topics than unpleasant ones.
How do daydreams affect daydreamers? A wandering mind leaves us vulnerable when driving. In one study, researchers interviewed 955 people involved in traffic accidents. The majority of them reported having daydreamed just before the accident.
Yet other research suggests that daydreaming has benefits. Researchers have found that it gives us a chance to think about our goals and it also seems to increase creativity. In one experiment, 145 undergraduates completed four "unusual uses" tasks, each requiring them to list as many uses as possible for an everyday object. After the first pair of tasks was completed, one group of participants was assigned an undemanding activity intended to cause their minds to wander. When all the participants proceeded to the second pair of tasks, the daydreamers performed 40 percent better than the others.

groups.title: Section C · 第 1 篇 · 16–18 题
groups.material:
Dating from as far back as the 12th century, they are claimed to be the rarest historic buildings in western Europe. These buildings offer vital insight into Scandinavia's Viking past. But now, with only 30 wooden churches remaining and their condition deteriorating, experts are working to preserve the structures for future generations.
Some of these spectacular churches are no more than small buildings, barely 4 metres wide and 6 metres tall. Others are much larger structures. They soar up to 40 metres into the cold air. Most consist of timber frames that rest on stone blocks. This means that they have no foundations. Although many of the churches appear from the outside to be complex structures, they normally feature only a single storey but numerous different roof levels.
Staff from the Norwegian government have carried out conservation work on 10 of the churches over the past two years. Most of these churches date from between the 12th and 14th centuries. Other churches were conserved in previous years. So far, specialists have worked to add preservative materials to the churches' exteriors. They also replaced rotting roofs and halted the sinking of the churches into the ground. In two cases, huge machines have been used to lift the buildings up to 30 centimetres into the air. This was accomplished so that the team could examine and repair the churches' original medieval stone blocks. The team plans to return to around a dozen of the buildings to assess progress and consider further action.
The earliest free-standing wooden church was probably built in Norway in around 1080. However, the largest known wooden churches were built from the 1130s onwards. This period was one of inter-elite rivalry in which nobles sought to increase their influence by funding the construction of churches and other buildings.
The reason for constructing the buildings from wood is probably that ideally proportioned straight and slender timber was available in large quantities in Scandinavia's vast pine forests. As wood was so plentiful, it was cheaper to use than the stone used in the buildings of other European cultures. The area's ship-building tradition, partly established by the Vikings, also meant that sophisticated carpentry was a major aspect of the local culture. The complex style of the medieval wooden church carvings, and the skills used to make them, almost certainly derive from the ancient Viking tradition.

groups.title: Section C · 第 2 篇 · 19–21 题
groups.material:
In last week's lecture, we discussed the characteristics of the newly born offspring of several mammals. You probably remember that human infants are less developed physically than other mammals of the same age. But in today's lecture, we'll look at three very interesting studies that hint at the surprising abilities of human babies.
In the first study, three-year-olds watched two videos shown side by side, each featuring a different researcher, one of whom they'd met once two years earlier. The children spent longer watching the video showing the researcher they hadn't met. This is consistent with young children's usual tendency to look longer at things that aren't familiar. And really this is amazing. It suggests the children remembered the researcher they'd met just one time when they were only one-year-olds. Of course, as most of us forget memories from our first few years as we grow older, these early long-term memories will likely be lost in subsequent years.
Our second study is about music. For this study, researchers played music to babies through speakers located on either side of a human face. They waited until the babies got bored and averted their gaze from the face. And then they changed the mood of the music, either from sad to happy or the other way around. This mood switch made no difference to the three-month-olds; but for the nine-month-olds, it was enough to renew their interest and they started looking again in the direction of the face. This suggests that babies of that age can tell the difference between a happy melody and a sad tune.
Our final study is from 1980, but it's still relevant today. In fact, it's one of the most famous pieces of research about infant emotion ever published. The study involved ordinary adults watching video clips of babies nine months or younger. In the video clips, the babies made various facial expressions in response to real-life events including playful interactions and painful ones. The adult observers were able to reliably discern an assortment of emotions on the babies' faces. These emotions included interest, joy, surprise, sadness, anger, disgust, contempt, and fear.
Next week, we'll be looking at this last study more closely. In fact, we will be viewing some of the video clips from that study. And together, see how well we do in discerning the babies' emotions.

groups.title: Section C · 第 3 篇 · 22–25 题
groups.material:
Today I'd like to talk about the dangers of being too collaborative. Being a good team player is an essential skill in our modern workplace. The ability to work well with others and collaborate on projects is a sought-after ability in nearly every position. However, placing too much emphasis on being a good team player can negatively affect your career growth.
Don't be overly focused on gaining consensus. Don't be too concerned with the opinions of others. This can hinder your ability to make decisions, speak up, and gain recognition for your individual skills and strengths. Some people are too subordinate to others' opinions, too focused on decision consensus, too silent about their own point of view, too agreeable to take things on when they don't have time or energy. This leads to building a brand of underconfident, submissive, low-impact non-leaders and hampers their growth and career advancement.
Collaboration certainly makes your individual competencies and contributions more difficult for outsiders to identify. Collaborative projects mean you're sharing the spotlight with others. Outsiders may then find it difficult to determine your contributions and strengths. This may end up costing you opportunities for promotions or pay raises.
You certainly shouldn't ditch teamwork, but how can you avoid the hazards of being an over-collaborator?
Working in a team can have huge benefits. Your team may have repeated successes and often gain recognition. You then have more opportunities to expand your professional network than if you worked alone. However, finding a balance between team efforts and individual projects that give you independent recognition is important for making a name for yourself and providing opportunities for advancement.
Be selective in who you work with. This will maximize the benefits and minimize the downsides of being a team player. Collaborate with people who have complementary expertise. Select projects where there's potential for mutual benefit. Perhaps you're bringing your unique knowledge and gaining access to someone else's professional network. Or maybe you're able to learn a new skill by working with someone. Seek out your teammates purposefully rather than jumping on every new group project opportunity.
When we're too collaborative, we want everyone to agree with a decision before we proceed. This can create unnecessary delays as you hold meetings trying to achieve a consensus. It's fine to be collaborative when seeking input, but put a deadline on the input stage and arrive at a decision, even if it's a decision that doesn't have consensus.

questions.explanation:
【题目】 What is the woman's profession? 

 【翻译】 这位女士的职业是什么？ 
 A)  杂志记者 
 B)  时装设计师 
 C)  网站设计师 
 D)  专题编辑 

 【答案】 D （细节题） Features editor 
 【定位】 P1 Today our guest is Rosie Mullender, who works as Features Editor for Fashion magazine. 
 今天我们的嘉宾是罗西·穆兰德，她在《时尚》杂志担任专题编辑。 

 【信号】 主持人开场介绍即报职务 。答案信号是开场白里主持人直接介绍嘉宾身份：who works as Features Editor for Fashion magazine，works as 后面紧跟的就是职务名，是身份题最稳的落点。 

 【替换】 works as Features Editor ↔ Features editor 职务名几乎原样对应 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 录音确实念到 Fashion magazine，选项 Magazine reporter 借这个"杂志"原词诱你选，但她是"编辑 editor"不是"记者 reporter"，职务对不上。  借用原文：Fashion magazine 

 B) 原词陷阱 录音里 Fashion 是杂志的名字（Fashion magazine），选项 Fashion designer 借这个 Fashion 让你误以为她是"时尚设计师"，但她的工作是当编辑，不是做服装设计。  借用原文：Fashion magazine 

 C) 原词陷阱 录音后面提到为杂志和网站写稿 writing copy for the magazine and website，选项 Website designer 借这个 website 诱选，但"为网站写稿"不等于"网站设计师"，职务完全两回事。  借用原文：writing copy for the magazine and website

 很多人认为在杂志社工作是一份光鲜亮丽的工作。这是对你工作的准确写照吗？

questions.prompt: What helped the woman to get her current position?
options: Her persistence
Her experience

questions.explanation:
【题目】 What helped the woman to get her current position? 

 【翻译】 是什么帮助这位女士获得了她目前的职位？ 
 A)  她的坚持不懈 
 B)  她的经验 
 C)  她的能力 
 D)  她的自信 

 【答案】 A （细节题） Her persistence 
 【定位】 P10 I had to be really persistent and it was very hard work. 
 我必须非常坚持不懈，而且要付出非常艰辛的努力。 

 【信号】 被问者直接应答里的强调词 。答案信号是她对"如何克服困难"这一问的直接应答开头：I had to be really persistent，really 加重语气强调 persistent（坚持不懈），是她明确点出的成功关键。 

 【替换】 I had to be really persistent ↔ Her persistence 形容词 persistent 名词化为 persistence 

 【排除】 B) 原词陷阱 录音末句确有 experience：all experiences make you a better journalist，选项 Her experience 借这个原词诱选，但那句是说"各种经历会让你成为更好的记者"这一信念，并非她把"经验"当成拿到这份工作的直接原因，真正帮她的是"坚持"。  借用原文：all experiences make you a better journalist 

 C) 未提及 Her competence（能力）与"坚持"都是褒义品质、意思相近极易混，但录音通篇没说是"能力"帮了她，她明确强调的是 persistent，competence 属编造。 
 D) 未提及 Her confidence（自信）也是褒义品质，听着像励志故事该有的词，但录音里她强调的是 really persistent"坚持"，从未说靠"自信"，属编造。

questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the man think of the satire Frankie he recently watched? 

 【翻译】 男士对他最近看的讽刺剧 Frankie 有什么看法? 
 A)  它很有趣。 
 B)  它很有教育意义。 
 C)  它脱离现实生活。 
 D)  它改编自一部戏剧。 

 【答案】 A （态度观点题） It is enjoyable. 
 【定位】 P2 I'm watching a great satire called Frankie. I think you'd like it. 
 我在看一部很棒的讽刺剧，叫《Frankie》。我想你会喜欢它的。 

 【信号】 评价形容词 great 。男士一开口就用 a great satire 给出正面评价，great 这个评价形容词就是答案信号；后面 I think you'd like it 进一步印证他态度是正面的。 

 【替换】 a great satire ↔ It is enjoyable. great 同义于 enjoyable 

 【排除】 B) 过度推断 It is educational. 把好评具体化成『有教育意义』，但录音通篇只说它 great、funny，从没提它能教人东西，属过度推断。 
 C) 原词陷阱 It is divorced from real life. 借了录音里 is divorced 的 divorced，但原文 divorced 指剧中人物『离婚』，根本不是说这剧『脱离现实』；且这是负评，与男士的正面态度相反。  借用原文：is divorced 

 D) 原词陷阱 It is adapted from a drama. 借了录音 a mixture of comedy and drama 里的 drama，但原文是说这剧『混合了喜剧与正剧元素』，不是说它『改编自某部戏剧』；而且本题问态度，这是来源描述，答非所问。  借用原文：a mixture of comedy and drama

questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the man say is special about the satire Frankie? 

 【翻译】 男士说讽刺剧 Frankie 有什么特别之处? 
 A)  所有角色都由著名演员出演。 
 B)  它根据一些名人的真实生活经历改编。 
 C)  它的情节和事件揭示了很多 Frankie 的真实生活。 
 D)  它由 Frankie 本人编剧、导演、剪辑和制作。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） It is written, directed, edited and produced by Frankie himself 
 【定位】 P8 In fact, the whole show is written, directed, edited and produced by him, and is very funny and has won many awards. 
 事实上，整部剧都是由他一人编剧、导演、剪辑和制作的，非常好笑，还赢得了很多奖项。 

 【信号】 强调词 In fact 。上一句女士说这是个 very original concept（很新颖的概念），男士用 In fact, the whole show is written, directed, edited and produced by him 接上，In fact 是强调信号，引出这剧『特别』的核心——一人全包。 

 【替换】 written, directed, edited and produced by him ↔ written, directed, edited and produced by Frankie himself him 即 Frankie himself 

 【排除】 A) 与原文相反 All the roles are played by famous actors and actresses. 与原文相反：录音说 all his friends and family are played by actors，只是普通 actors，且明确主角 he plays himself，并非『所有角色都由名演员演』。  借用原文：all his friends and family are played by actors 

 B) 原词陷阱 It is based on the real-life experiences of some celebrities. 借了录音 a real-life series about a real person 的 real-life，但原文随即被男士否定（It's fiction），且只涉及 Frankie 一人，不是 some celebrities，主体与真假都对不上。  借用原文：a real-life series about a real person 

 C) 与原文相反 Its plots and events reveal a lot about Frankie's actual life. 把原文借来的『真实生活』安在情节上，但录音说 the plots and events that take place are also invented——情节是虚构的，恰恰不反映真实生活，正好说反。  借用原文：the plots and events that take place are also invented

questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the woman say she is going to do with the satire Frankie? 

 【翻译】 女士说她打算如何处理讽刺剧 Frankie? 
 A)  去影院观看它。 
 B)  把它推荐给她的朋友们。 
 C)  和男士一起看它。 
 D)  下载并观看它。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） Download and watch it. 
 【定位】 P9 That's cool. I will try to download it. 
 真酷。我会试着把它下载下来看。 

 【信号】 意向句 I will 。女士用 I will try to download it 直接表态自己的打算，I will 是表意向的信号词，紧跟的动作 download 就是答案。 

 【替换】 I will try to download it ↔ Download and watch it. download 即下载来看 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 Go to the theater and enjoy it. 录音从未提到女士要去剧院看，她说的是下载，属无中生有。 
 B) 张冠李戴 Recommend it to her friends. 像是把男士那句 I think you'd like it（推荐给女士）的『推荐』动作挪到女士头上，但女士本人只说要下载，没说要推荐给朋友。  借用原文：I think you'd like it 

 C) 原词陷阱 Watch it with the man. 里 watch 确是原文反复出现的词，但录音里女士只说自己下载来看，全程没有『和男士一起看』的安排，with the man 是凭空添加。  借用原文：then you should check it out

questions.prompt: What does the woman say about the comedy The Big Bang Theory?
options: It has drawn criticisms from scientists.
It has been showing for over a decade.
It is a ridiculous piece of satire.
It is against common sense.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the woman say about the comedy The Big Bang Theory? 

 【翻译】 女士对喜剧《生活大爆炸》有什么评价? 
 A)  它遭到了科学家们的批评。 
 B)  它已经播出了十多年。 
 C)  它是一部荒谬的讽刺作品。 
 D)  它违背常识。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） It has been showing for over a decade. 
 【定位】 P11 The show has been running for over ten years, and some of the actors are practically global superstars, now that they are such famous celebrities. 
 这部剧已经播了十多年，其中一些演员实际上已成了全球超级巨星，如今他们都是大名鼎鼎的明星了。 

 【信号】 并列陈述里的事实 。女士在 some of the actors are practically global superstars, now that they are such famous celebrities 里给出一条客观事实——部分演员已成名人；这种可核对的事实陈述就是细节题的答案落点。 

 【替换】 some of the actors are practically global superstars, now that they are such famous celebrities ↔ It is based on the real-life experiences of some celebrities. 演员成名人对应 celebrities 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 It has drawn criticisms from scientists. 借了录音 four male scientists 的 scientists，但原文只是说剧里有四个科学家角色，从没说这剧『招来科学家批评』，批评是无中生有。  借用原文：four male scientists 

 C) 张冠李戴 It is a ridiculous piece of satire. 里 satire 是男士形容《Frankie》的词（a great satire），并非女士对《The Big Bang Theory》的评价；况且女士说它 very funny、a huge hit，从无 ridiculous 之贬。  借用原文：a great satire 

 D) 与原文相反 It is against common sense. 盗用录音 the lady's social skills and common sense 的 common sense，但原文是说那位女士『有 common sense（常识）』，根本不是说这部剧『违背常识』，意思正好相反。  借用原文：the lady's social skills and common sense

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say about players of contact sports?
options: They are likely to get injured when moving too fast.
They believe in team spirit for good performance.
They need to keep moving to avoid getting hurt.
They have to learn how to avoid body contact.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the speaker say about players of contact sports? 

 【翻译】 说话者关于接触性运动的运动员说了什么? 
 A)  他们在移动过快时很可能受伤。 
 B)  他们相信团队精神能带来良好表现。 
 C)  他们需要保持移动以避免受伤。 
 D)  他们必须学习如何避免身体接触。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） They need to keep moving to avoid getting hurt. 
 【定位】 P2 Those who play contact sports know that the player who usually gets hurt the most is the one who is standing still. 
 从事身体接触类运动的人都知道，通常受伤最重的，恰恰是那个站着不动的人。 

 【信号】 出现题干同款话题词 contact sports，其后即答案 。录音里 Those who play contact sports 与题干 contact sports 完全同词，是顺听定位的信号灯；说话人讲到这个话题词后紧接的判断 the player who usually gets hurt the most is the one who is standing still 就是答案句。 

 【替换】 the player who usually gets hurt the most is the one who is standing still ↔ They need to keep moving to avoid getting hurt. '站着不动的人最受伤'反过来即'要保持移动才不受伤' 

 【排除】 A) 与原文相反 They are likely to get injured when moving too fast. 把受伤怪到'移动太快'头上，而原文说受伤最重的是 the one who is standing still——是'不动'受伤，不是'动太快'受伤，方向恰好反了。  借用原文：the player who usually gets hurt the most is the one who is standing still 

 B) 未提及 They believe in team spirit for good performance. 讲'团队精神'，但录音谈接触类运动只说了'不动的人最易受伤'，全程没出现 team spirit 或团队配合的内容，属凭'运动→团队'常识硬填。 
 D) 原词陷阱 They have to learn how to avoid body contact. 里的 body contact 借了原文 Those who play contact sports 的 contact 一词，但原文是说'接触类运动里不动的人最受伤'，从没说要去'避免身体接触'，是听到 contact 就想选的原词陷阱。  借用原文：Those who play contact sports

questions.prompt: What do longevity statistics reveal about the average person?
options: They do not have many years to live after retirement.
They tend to live a longer life with early retirement.
They do not start enjoying life until full retirement.
They keep themselves busy even after retirement.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do longevity statistics reveal about the average person? 

 【翻译】 寿命统计数据揭示了关于普通人的什么信息? 
 A)  他们退休后没有多少年可活。 
 B)  他们往往因提早退休而活得更长。 
 C)  他们直到完全退休才开始享受生活。 
 D)  他们即使退休后也让自己保持忙碌。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） They do not have many years to live after retirement. 
 【定位】 P3 Longevity statistics reveal that the average person doesn't last very long after retirement. 
 寿命统计数据显示，普通人在退休之后活不了多久。 

 【信号】 题干锚词 statistics reveal 在原文原样出现，紧跟即答案 。录音 Longevity statistics reveal 与题干用词完全一致，是定位信号；其后宾语从句 the average person doesn't last very long after retirement 就是统计数据揭示的内容，即答案句。 

 【替换】 the average person doesn't last very long after retirement ↔ They do not have many years to live after retirement. '活不了多久'＝'没有多少年可活' 

 【排除】 B) 与原文相反 They tend to live a longer life with early retirement. 说早退休反而更长寿，而原文是 the average person doesn't last very long after retirement——退休后活不久，且后文紧接 The moral here is don't retire，劝人别退休；选项把原文意思反了过来。  借用原文：the average person doesn't last very long after retirement 

 C) 原词陷阱 They do not start enjoying life until full retirement. 借了原文反复出现的 retirement，造出'要等完全退休才开始享受生活'，但原文谈退休只说'活不久、别退休'，根本没谈'何时开始享受生活'，是借原词的答非所问。  借用原文：the average person doesn't last very long after retirement 

 D) 张冠李戴 They keep themselves busy even after retirement. 与全篇 keep moving、stay involved 主题字面相符，借了主旨词诱选；但本题问的是'统计数据揭示普通人怎样'，答案是'退休后活不久'，而非描述他们'退休后仍忙碌'，张冠李戴。  借用原文：that is how he got to be 94, by staying involved

questions.prompt: What bonus does the "keep moving" principle bring us according to the speaker?
options: It prevents us from worrying.
It slows down our aging process.
It enables us to accomplish more in life.
It provides us with more chances to learn.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What bonus does the "keep moving" principle bring us according to the speaker? 

 【翻译】 根据说话者所说,"保持移动"原则给我们带来了什么额外好处? 
 A)  它使我们免于担忧。 
 B)  它减缓我们的衰老过程。 
 C)  它使我们能够在人生中成就更多。 
 D)  它为我们提供更多学习机会。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） It prevents us from worrying. 
 【定位】 P4 A bonus with the "keep moving" principle is that while we keep moving, we don't have a chance to worry. 
 "保持移动"原则带来的一个额外好处是：当我们不停活动时，就没有机会去忧虑。 

 【信号】 题干同款词 a bonus 领起，正是好处提示句 。录音 A bonus with the "keep moving" principle is that 与题干 bonus 完全同词，是定位信号；其后 while we keep moving, we don't have a chance to worry 即点出好处，为答案句。 

 【替换】 we don't have a chance to worry ↔ It prevents us from worrying. '没机会去忧虑'＝'防止我们忧虑' 

 【排除】 B) 未提及 It slows down our aging process. 在养生话题里很顺耳，但本题答案句说的好处是 we don't have a chance to worry，全文也没说 keep moving 能 slow down aging，是用常识硬填的未提及项。 
 C) 答非所问 It enables us to accomplish more in life. 借了前文名人成就(写作、获奖、作画到八九十岁)的语境联想，但那是第 3 段讲长寿的例子，本题问的是第 4 段的 bonus，而 bonus 明确是'没机会担忧'，并非'让人成就更多'，答非所问。  借用原文：Benjamin Franklin produced some of his best writings at the age of 84 

 D) 原词陷阱 It provides us with more chances to learn. 借了第 2 段 keep moving, extending and learning 里的 learning，但那是讲 keep moving 的内涵、不是第 4 段问的 bonus；本题 bonus 是'没空担忧'，与'更多学习机会'无关，是听到 learn 就想选的原词陷阱。  借用原文：the essential message is "keep moving, extending and learning."
questions.spoken_text: What bonus does the keep moving principal bring us according to the speaker?

questions.prompt: What does the passage say about people's mind?
options: It tends to dwell upon their joyous experiences.
It wanders for almost half of their waking time.
It has trouble concentrating after a brain injury.
It tends to be affected by their negative feelings.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the passage say about people's mind? 

 【翻译】 文章关于人们的思维说了什么? 
 A)  它倾向于停留在他们快乐的经历上。 
 B)  它在他们醒着的时间里有近一半时间在游离。 
 C)  它在脑部受伤后难以集中注意力。 
 D)  它往往会受到他们负面情绪的影响。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） It wanders for almost half of their waking time. 
 【定位】 P1 By one estimate, people daydream through nearly half of their waking hours. 
 据某项估计，人们在将近一半的清醒时间里都在走神（做白日梦）。 

 【信号】 数字估计句即落点 。本句以 By one estimate（据估计）领出一个量化结论 nearly half of their waking hours，篇章里凡跟着 "据估计/研究发现" 的量化句，往往就是承载答案的总述句，是听力定位的强信号。 

 【替换】 daydream through nearly half of their waking hours ↔ wanders for almost half of their waking time daydream=wanders、hours≈time 同义改写 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 A 说大脑 dwell upon their joyous experiences（沉湎于愉快经历），看似呼应原文 more likely to wander toward pleasant topics，但那是讲走神时偏向愉快话题、并非本题问的 "大脑总体特点"，属答非所问，且 "沉湎/dwell upon" 原文也未说。  借用原文：They were more likely to wander toward pleasant topics than unpleasant ones. 

 C) 未提及 C 说大脑 trouble concentrating after a brain injury（脑损伤后难以集中），原文全篇讲的是走神（mind wandering）与白日梦，从未提到 brain injury（脑损伤）这回事，属凭空捏造。 
 D) 原词陷阱 D 说大脑 affected by their negative feelings（受负面情绪影响），借用了原文 wander more when they felt upset（心烦时更易走神）里的 upset，但原文是说 "走神频率" 受情绪影响、且偏向愉快话题，并非笼统说大脑被负面情绪左右，是把局部信息夸大、错置到本题。  借用原文：Respondents' minds tended to wander more when they felt upset rather than happy.
questions.spoken_text: what does the passage say about people's mind?

questions.prompt: For what purpose did the researchers develop the new app?
options: To find how happiness relates to daydreaming.
To observe how one's mind affects one's behavior.
To see why daydreaming impacts what one is doing.
To study the relation between health and daydreaming.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 For what purpose did the researchers develop the new app? 

 【翻译】 研究人员开发这款新应用的目的是什么? 
 A)  发现幸福感与白日梦的关系。 
 B)  观察一个人的思维如何影响其行为。 
 C)  了解白日梦为何影响一个人正在做的事情。 
 D)  研究健康与白日梦之间的关系。 

 【答案】 A （目的题） To find how happiness relates to daydreaming. 
 【定位】 P2 For one experiment, researchers developed an app to analyze the relationship between daydreaming and happiness. 
 在一项实验中，研究人员开发了一款应用程序，用来分析白日梦（走神）与幸福之间的关系。 

 【信号】 to do 即目的落点 。句中 developed an app to analyze the relationship between daydreaming and happiness 用 to analyze 直接交代开发 app 的目的，目的状语 to do 后面跟的就是答案，是目的题最硬的定位信号。 

 【替换】 to analyze the relationship between daydreaming and happiness ↔ To find how happiness relates to daydreaming analyze the relationship=find how…relates 同义 

 【排除】 B) 原词陷阱 B 说目的是 To observe how one's mind affects one's behavior（观察心智如何影响行为），借用了原文反复出现的 mind 一词，但原文 app 是分析 "走神与幸福" 的关系，并非 "心智与行为" 的关系，宾语被偷换。  借用原文：to analyze the relationship between daydreaming and happiness 

 C) 原词陷阱 C 说目的是 To see why daydreaming impacts what one is doing（看走神为何影响手头的事），其中 "走神影响手头的事" 呼应了原文 think about something other than the task one is doing，但那是前文对走神现象的定义，不是开发 app 的目的，属答非所问。  借用原文：the tendency to think about something other than the task one is doing 

 D) 偷换概念 D 说目的是研究 the relation between health and daydreaming（健康与走神的关系），把原文的 happiness（幸福）偷换成读音相近的 health（健康），其余几乎照搬，是最贴近正确项、最易听岔的陷阱。  借用原文：the relationship between daydreaming and happiness
questions.spoken_text: For what purpose did the researchers develop the new app?

questions.prompt: How does daydreaming benefit people according to some researchers?
options: It helps them make good decisions.
It helps them tap their potentials.
It contributes to their creativity.
It contributes to clear thinking
questions.explanation:
【题目】 How does daydreaming benefit people according to some researchers? 

 【翻译】 根据一些研究人员的说法,白日梦如何使人们受益? 
 A)  它帮助他们做出正确的决定。 
 B)  它帮助他们发掘自己的潜力。 
 C)  它有助于他们的创造力。 
 D)  它有助于清晰思考。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） It contributes to their creativity. 
 【定位】 P4 Yet other research suggests that daydreaming has benefits. Researchers have found that it gives us a chance to think about our goals and it also seems to increase creativity. 
 然而另一些研究表明，走神（白日梦）也有好处。研究人员发现，它让我们有机会思考自己的目标，似乎还能提升创造力。 

 【信号】 转折Yet后才是好处 。本段以 Yet 转折，把前文走神的坏处（开车走神出事故）一转，转折后才是本题要的好处；篇章里 yet / but / however 之后的内容常是真正落点，听到转折词要立刻提起注意。 

 【替换】 it also seems to increase creativity ↔ It contributes to their creativity increase=contributes to 同义 

 【排除】 A) 过度推断 A 说走神帮人 make good decisions（做好决定），看似贴近原文 think about our goals（思考目标），但 "思考目标" 不等于 "做好决定"，原文只说给机会想目标，没说由此能做好决策，属过度推断。  借用原文：it gives us a chance to think about our goals 

 B) 未提及 B 说走神帮人 tap their potentials（发掘潜能），原文讲到的好处只有 "思考目标" 和 "提升创造力"，从未提及 potential（潜能），属凭空添加。 
 D) 未提及 D 说走神带来 clear thinking（清晰的思考），原文列的好处是 think about goals 与 increase creativity，并无 "使思考更清晰" 之说，属无中生有的近义干扰。
questions.spoken_text: How does daydreaming benefit people according to some researchers?

questions.prompt: What was the finding of the experiment with 145 undergraduates?
options: Subjects with clear goals in mind outperformed those without clear goals.
The difference in performance between the two groups was insignificant.
Non-daydreamers were more focused on their tasks than daydreamers.
Daydreamers did better than non-daydreamers in task performance.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What was the finding of the experiment with 145 undergraduates? 

 【翻译】 对145名本科生进行的实验有什么发现? 
 A)  目标明确的受试者表现优于没有明确目标的受试者。 
 B)  两组之间的表现差异不显著。 
 C)  非白日梦者比白日梦者更专注于他们的任务。 
 D)  白日梦者在任务表现上优于非白日梦者。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） Daydreamers did better than non-daydreamers in task performance. 
 【定位】 P4 When all the participants proceeded to the second pair of tasks, the daydreamers performed 40 percent better than the others. 
 当所有受试者进行第二组任务时，走神（做白日梦）的那一组比其他人表现好了百分之四十。 

 【信号】 比较+百分比即结论 。句中 performed 40 percent better than the others 是带百分比的比较句，出现在整段实验描述的最后，正是实验结论；实验题里 "X% better than""outperformed" 这类末尾比较句就是答案信号。 

 【替换】 the daydreamers performed 40 percent better than the others ↔ Daydreamers did better than non-daydreamers in task performance performed better=did better、the others=non-daydreamers 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 A 说 Subjects with clear goals in mind outperformed those without clear goals（有明确目标者胜过无目标者），把分组标准说成 "有无清晰目标"，但本实验分组是 "被安排走神 vs 没被安排"，且 goals 一词来自第4段前文 think about our goals 而非本实验，属张冠李戴的捏造。  借用原文：it gives us a chance to think about our goals 

 B) 与原文相反 B 说两组 The difference in performance between the two groups was insignificant（差异不显著），而原文明说差了 40 percent better——这是巨大差异，B 与原文结论完全相反。  借用原文：the daydreamers performed 40 percent better than the others 

 C) 与原文相反 C 说 Non-daydreamers were more focused on their tasks than daydreamers（非走神者比走神者更专注于任务），把胜出方向反过来了——原文是 daydreamers 表现更好，且原文讲的是 "表现" 而非 "专注度"，方向和维度都错。  借用原文：the daydreamers performed 40 percent better than the others
questions.spoken_text: What was the finding of the experiment with 145 undergraduates?

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say about the Viking wooden churches?
options: They are the oldest buildings in Europe.
They are part of the Christian tradition.
They are renovated to attract tourists.
They are in worsening condition.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the speaker say about the Viking wooden churches? 

 【翻译】 说话者对维京木制教堂有何评价？ 
 A)  它们是欧洲最古老的建筑。 
 B)  它们是基督教传统的一部分。 
 C)  它们经过翻新以吸引游客。 
 D)  它们的状况正在恶化。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） They are in worsening condition. 
 【定位】 P1 But now, with only 30 wooden churches remaining and their condition deteriorating, experts are working to preserve the structures for future generations. 
 但如今，仅存 30 座木教堂、且它们的状况正在恶化，专家们正努力为后代保护这些建筑。 

 【信号】 转折 But now 后才是真意 。前半句还在夸它们 the rarest historic buildings，一个 But now 把话锋转向现状，转折之后的 their condition deteriorating 才是说话人要落的点——听到 but now 就该把耳朵竖起来。 

 【替换】 their condition deteriorating ↔ in worsening condition deteriorating = worsening 同义改写 

 【排除】 A) 偷换概念 原文夸它们是 the rarest historic buildings in western Europe（最稀有），A 偷偷把 rarest 换成 oldest（最古老）——稀有不等于最古老，听到“最高级 + 西欧”就想选就中套了。  借用原文：the rarest historic buildings in western Europe 

 B) 过度推断 原文只说它们是 wooden churches（木教堂），借“教堂”让你脑补“基督教传统”，但全篇真正定调的是 Scandinavia's Viking past（维京渊源），从没把它们说成基督教传统的一部分，属过度推断。  借用原文：Scandinavia's Viking past 

 C) 未提及 原文说专家在 working to preserve the structures for future generations（为后代保护），C 却说成 renovated to attract tourists（为引客而翻新）——保护目的被换成招揽游客，原文根本没提 tourists，属无中生有。

questions.prompt: What is special about most of the Viking wooden churches?
options: They have a history of 14 centuries.
They are 40 metres tall on average.
They are without foundations.
They consist of several storeys.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What is special about most of the Viking wooden churches? 

 【翻译】 大多数维京木制教堂有何特别之处？ 
 A)  它们有14世纪的历史。 
 B)  它们平均高40米。 
 C)  它们没有地基。 
 D)  它们由多层构成。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） They are without foundations. 
 【定位】 P2 Most consist of timber frames that rest on stone blocks. This means that they have no foundations. 
 大多数教堂由架在石块上的木构架组成。这意味着它们没有地基。 

 【信号】 Most + This means 推出特征 。题干问的是 most（大多数），原文正以 Most consist of 开头，紧接一句 This means that they have no foundations 把特征点破——This means 后面的那句结论就是说话人要你抓的特别之处。 

 【替换】 they have no foundations ↔ without foundations have no = without 否定同义 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 原文说它们 Dating from as far back as the 12th century（最早可追到 12 世纪），A 把“12 世纪”歪算成“14 个世纪的历史”——12th century 是年代，14 centuries 是时长，听到数字就抓极易上当。  借用原文：Dating from as far back as the 12th century 

 B) 原词陷阱 原文说有些大的 soar up to 40 metres（最高可达 40 米），B 却说成 40 metres tall on average（平均高 40 米）——up to（至多）被偷换成 on average（平均），且这只描述“大的那些”不是 most。  借用原文：They soar up to 40 metres into the cold air 

 D) 与原文相反 原文明说它们 normally feature only a single storey（通常只有单层），D 却说 several storeys（好几层）——只是多了几个不同的屋顶层 roof levels，被偷换成“好几层楼”，与原文相反。  借用原文：they normally feature only a single storey but numerous different roof levels
questions.spoken_text: What is special about most of the Viking wooden churches?

questions.prompt: Why were the Viking churches constructed from wood?
options: Wood was harmonious with nature.
Wooden buildings kept the cold out.
Timber was abundant in Scandinavia.
The Vikings liked wooden structures.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 Why were the Viking churches constructed from wood? 

 【翻译】 维京教堂为何用木材建造？ 
 A)  木材与自然和谐共处。 
 B)  木制建筑能够御寒。 
 C)  斯堪的纳维亚木材资源丰富。 
 D)  维京人喜欢木质结构。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） Timber was abundant in Scandinavia. 
 【定位】 P5 The reason for constructing the buildings from wood is probably that ideally proportioned straight and slender timber was available in large quantities in Scandinavia's vast pine forests. 
 用木材建造这些建筑的原因，很可能是斯堪的纳维亚广袤的松林里盛产比例匀称、笔直纤细的木材。 

 【信号】 The reason…is 直接点原因 。原文用 The reason for constructing the buildings from wood is probably that 把原因明明白白引出来，后半句 available in large quantities 就是真因——“The reason…is”是最直白的因果信号，听到就锁。 

 【替换】 timber was available in large quantities in Scandinavia's vast pine forests ↔ Timber was abundant in Scandinavia. available in large quantities = abundant 概括 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 “木头与自然和谐”听着很顺，但原文给的原因是木材量大又便宜（cheaper to use than the stone），从没说过 harmonious with nature，属无中生有。 
 B) 未提及 原文只提到 the cold air（冷空气）描述教堂高耸的环境，B 借这个“冷”字脑补成“木建筑御寒”，但用木头的原因和保暖毫无关系，属未提及。  借用原文：They soar up to 40 metres into the cold air 

 D) 张冠李戴 原文里 Vikings 出现在“造船传统”和“雕刻技艺源自维京”的语境（partly established by the Vikings），D 却把它说成“维京人喜欢木结构”——用木的真因是“木材多又便宜”，把原因安到“维京偏好”头上，是张冠李戴。  借用原文：partly established by the Vikings
questions.spoken_text: Why were the Viking churches constructed from wood?

questions.prompt: What are the three interesting studies about?
options: Similarities between human babies and baby animals.
Cognitive features of different newly born mammals.
Adults' influence on children.
Abilities of human babies.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What are the three interesting studies about? 

 【翻译】 这三项有趣的研究是关于什么的? 
 A)  人类婴儿与动物幼崽之间的相似之处。 
 B)  不同新生哺乳动物的认知特征。 
 C)  成人对儿童的影响。 
 D)  人类婴儿的能力。 

 【答案】 D （主旨题） Abilities of human babies. 
 【定位】 P1 But in today's lecture, we'll look at three very interesting studies that hint at the surprising abilities of human babies. 
 但在今天的讲座里，我们将看三项非常有趣的研究，它们暗示了人类婴儿令人惊讶的能力。 

 【信号】 转折 But 后的点题句 。前一句先说上周讲的是哺乳动物、人类婴儿"physically less developed"，紧接着用 But in today's lecture 转折，转折之后才是今天的真正主题；篇章独白里开头的 But / Today 之后那句通常就是全篇点题句。 

 【替换】 the surprising abilities of human babies ↔ Abilities of human babies 去掉修饰的同义概括 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 录音开头说上周讨论过 the newly born offspring of several mammals 并把人类婴儿与其他哺乳动物作比，A 把"人类婴儿与动物幼崽的相似"当成今天主题，实际那是上周内容、且"相似"也非录音重点，是用旧话题骗"听到 babies 和 animals 就选"。  借用原文：we discussed the characteristics of the newly born offspring of several mammals 

 B) 原词陷阱 录音确有 other mammals of the same age 一语，B 借此把主题说成"不同新生哺乳动物的认知特征"，但今天三项研究全讲人类婴儿、哺乳动物只是引子，这是把范围错放到了哺乳动物身上。  借用原文：human infants are less developed physically than other mammals of the same age 

 C) 未提及 C 说三项研究是关于"成人对孩子的影响"，但录音三项研究分别讲婴儿的记忆、辨乐、情绪，全程没有"成人影响孩子"这一主题（第四项里成人只是观察者），属凭空捏造。

questions.prompt: What does the second study find about nine-month-old babies?
options: They can distinguish a happy tune from a sad one.
They love happy melodies more than sad ones.
They fall asleep easily while listening to music.
They are already sensitive to beats and rhythms.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the second study find about nine-month-old babies? 

 【翻译】 第二项研究关于九个月大的婴儿有什么发现? 
 A)  他们能够区分欢快的曲调和悲伤的曲调。 
 B)  他们更喜欢欢快的旋律而不是悲伤的旋律。 
 C)  他们在听音乐时很容易入睡。 
 D)  他们已经对节拍和节奏很敏感。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） They can distinguish a happy tune from a sad one. 
 【定位】 P3 This suggests that babies of that age can tell the difference between a happy melody and a sad tune. 
 这表明那个月龄的婴儿能够分辨欢快的旋律和悲伤的曲调。 

 【信号】 结论句 This suggests 。实验描述之后用 This suggests that 引出研究结论，研究发现题的答案几乎都落在 suggests / shows / found 这类结论句上，而不在前面的实验过程描述里。 

 【替换】 can tell the difference between a happy melody and a sad tune ↔ distinguish a happy tune from a sad one tell the difference=distinguish 

 【排除】 B) 原词陷阱 录音通篇讲的是婴儿"能分辨"快乐与悲伤的曲子，从未说他们"更喜欢快乐的"；B 借用了 happy / sad 这组录音真实出现的词，却把"能区分"偷换成"更偏爱欢快的"，是 A 的对立干扰。  借用原文：either from sad to happy or the other way around 

 C) 原词陷阱 录音里婴儿是"got bored and averted their gaze"（厌倦后移开视线），C 却说他们"听音乐容易睡着"；它借 music 这个真实话题词，编造了录音从未提到的"睡着"反应。  借用原文：They waited until the babies got bored and averted their gaze from the face 

 D) 未提及 D 说婴儿"对节拍和韵律敏感"，但本段只讲"能分辨快乐与悲伤的曲调"，从未提及 beats and rhythms；这是引入录音没有的新概念。

questions.prompt: What is the 1980 study about?
options: Infants' facial expressions.
Babies' emotions.
Babies' interaction with adult.
Infants' behaviors.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What is the 1980 study about? 

 【翻译】 1980年的研究是关于什么的? 
 A)  婴儿的面部表情。 
 B)  婴儿的情绪。 
 C)  婴儿与成人的互动。 
 D)  婴儿的行为。 

 【答案】 B （主旨题） Babies' emotions. 
 【定位】 P4 In fact, it's one of the most famous pieces of research about infant emotion ever published. 
 事实上，它是有史以来发表过的关于婴儿情绪的最著名研究之一。 

 【信号】 定性句 research about 。录音用 research about infant emotion 直接给这项研究下定义，about 后面的词就是研究主题；定性句优先于后文列举的表情、互动等具体环节。 

 【替换】 research about infant emotion ↔ Babies' emotions infant=baby、emotion同词 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 录音确实提到婴儿 made various facial expressions，A 借此说研究"关于面部表情"；但表情只是观察手段——成人通过看表情来判断情绪，研究真正的主题是"情绪"。这是最像对的原词陷阱。  借用原文：the babies made various facial expressions 

 C) 原词陷阱 录音说视频里的事件"including playful interactions"，C 借 interaction 说研究"关于婴儿与成人的互动"；但互动只是触发婴儿表情的情境之一，并非研究主题，且 C 还把它说成"与成人的互动"，偏离了研究核心。  借用原文：real-life events including playful interactions and painful ones 

 D) 偷换概念 D 用"婴儿的行为"这一最宽泛的词概括研究，但录音明确定性为关于"情绪"的研究，"行为"既未被录音用来定义这项研究、范围也过大，是以宽代窄的干扰。  借用原文：research about infant emotion

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say about being over collaborative?
options: It may harm the culture of today's workplace.
It may hinder individual career advancement.
It may result in unwillingness to take risks.
It may put too much pressure on team members.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the speaker say about being over collaborative? 

 【翻译】 说话者对过度合作有何看法? 
 A)  它可能损害当今职场的文化。 
 B)  它可能阻碍个人职业发展。 
 C)  它可能导致不愿承担风险。 
 D)  它可能给团队成员施加过大压力。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） It may hinder individual career advancement. 
 【定位】 P1 However, placing too much emphasis on being a good team player can negatively affect your career growth. 
 然而，过分强调做一个好的团队成员，会对你的职业成长产生负面影响。 

 【信号】 转折词 However 后才是真意 。前一句还在夸团队精神是必备技能，However, placing too much emphasis on being a good team player can negatively affect your career growth. 用 However 一转，才点出过度协作的核心危害——这句转折后的话就是答案句。 

 【替换】 negatively affect your career growth ↔ hinder individual career advancement negatively affect=hinder，career growth=career advancement 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 录音第一段确实念到 our modern workplace，A 项 It may harm the culture of today's workplace. 借这个 workplace 制造"听到就想选"的错觉，但原文从未说过过度协作会损害"职场文化"，危害对象是"你的职业成长"，不是文化。  借用原文：our modern workplace 

 C) 未提及 It may result in unwillingness to take risks. 说的"导致不愿冒险"在录音里找不到任何对应表述，是凭"过度协作好像会让人保守"的常识硬推出来的。 
 D) 原词陷阱 It may put too much pressure on team members. 套着"团队成员"这个全篇高频语境，但原文讲的危害是"拖累你自己的发展"，从没说过"给团队成员太大压力"，方向答非所问。  借用原文：being a good team player

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say about people engaged in collaborative projects?
options: They can hardly give expression to their original views.
They can become less motivated to do projects of their own.
They may find it hard to get their contributions recognized.
They may eventually lose their confidence and creativity
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the speaker say about people engaged in collaborative projects? 

 【翻译】 说话者对参与合作项目的人有何看法? 
 A)  他们几乎无法表达自己的原创观点。 
 B)  他们做自己项目的动力可能会降低。 
 C)  他们可能发现自己的贡献难以获得认可。 
 D)  他们最终可能失去信心和创造力。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） They may find it hard to get their contributions recognized. 
 【定位】 P3 Collaboration certainly makes your individual competencies and contributions more difficult for outsiders to identify. Collaborative projects mean you're sharing the spotlight with others. Outsiders may then find it difficult to determine your contributions and strengths. 
 协作确实会让外人更难看清你个人的能力与贡献。协作项目意味着你要和别人分享聚光灯。于是外人可能很难判断出你的贡献和长处。 

 【信号】 围绕 contributions 反复强调的核心句 。这一段三句都在说同一件事——more difficult for outsiders to identify、Outsiders may then find it difficult to determine your contributions and strengths.，反复强调"贡献被外人难以识别"，这种重复正是答案落点。 

 【替换】 Outsiders may then find it difficult to determine your contributions and strengths ↔ They may find it hard to get their contributions recognized outsiders determine your contributions=get contributions recognized 

 【排除】 A) 张冠李戴 They can hardly give expression to their original views. 像第二段"too silent about their own point of view"的影子，但那段讲的是"过度迁就者"，不是本题问的"做协作项目的人"，且本题答案句明确在讲"贡献难被识别"，与"表达观点"不是一回事。  借用原文：too silent about their own point of view 

 B) 未提及 They can become less motivated to do projects of their own. 把"积极性下降、不愿做个人项目"当后果，但录音第三段只讲"贡献难被外人看清"，从没说协作会让人"丧失做个人项目的动力"，属凭推测添加。 
 D) 过度推断 They may eventually lose their confidence and creativity 里 confidence 与第二段 underconfident 沾边，但那是讲过度迁就者的"品牌形象"，本题答案句根本没提 confidence 或 creativity，且 eventually lose 把后果夸到"丧失"，是过度推断。  借用原文：underconfident

questions.prompt: How do people benefit from working in a team?
options: They can enlarge their professional circle.
They can get chances to engage in research.
They can make the best use of their expertise.
They can complete the project more easily.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 How do people benefit from working in a team? 

 【翻译】 人们如何从团队工作中受益? 
 A)  他们可以扩大自己的职业圈子。 
 B)  他们可以获得参与研究的机会。 
 C)  他们可以充分利用自己的专长。 
 D)  他们可以更轻松地完成项目。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） They can enlarge their professional circle. 
 【定位】 P5 You then have more opportunities to expand your professional network than if you worked alone. 
 于是相比单干，你会有更多机会去扩展自己的职业人脉网络。 

 【信号】 benefits 后列举的具体好处句 。本段以 Working in a team can have huge benefits 开头点出"团队有大好处"，随后 more opportunities to expand your professional network 就是它列出的那条具体好处——益处总起句之后紧跟的具体项即答案。 

 【替换】 expand your professional network ↔ enlarge their professional circle expand=enlarge，network=circle 

 【排除】 B) 未提及 They can get chances to engage in research. 里的 research 在整篇录音里从未出现，是凭空添加的好处。 
 C) 原词陷阱 expertise 确在第六段念过（Collaborate with people who have complementary expertise），C 项 They can make the best use of their expertise. 借此诱选，但那段讲的是"如何挑选合作对象"，且原文是"找互补专长的人"，不是"用好自己的专长"，答非所问。  借用原文：complementary expertise 

 D) 未提及 They can complete the project more easily. 听上去"人多好办事"很顺，但录音讲团队好处时只提"重复的成功、被认可、扩展人脉"，从没说"项目能更轻松完成"，是常识脑补。

questions.prompt: Why is it undesirable to spend too much time trying to reach consensus?
options: It may cause lots of arguments in a team.
It may prevent making a timely decision.
It may give rise to a lot of unnecessary expenses.
It may deprive a team of business opportunities.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 Why is it undesirable to spend too much time trying to reach consensus? 

 【翻译】 为什么花费过多时间试图达成共识是不可取的? 
 A)  它可能在团队中引发大量争论。 
 B)  它可能妨碍及时做出决策。 
 C)  它可能产生大量不必要的开支。 
 D)  它可能剥夺团队的商业机会。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） It may prevent making a timely decision. 
 【定位】 P7 When we're too collaborative, we want everyone to agree with a decision before we proceed. This can create unnecessary delays as you hold meetings trying to achieve a consensus. 
 当我们过度协作时，我们想在推进前让每个人都同意某个决定。这会造成不必要的拖延，因为你要不停开会去达成共识。 

 【信号】 因果句 This can create…+ delays 是后果落点 。This can create unnecessary delays as you hold meetings trying to achieve a consensus. 用 This can create…直接给出"耗时求共识"的后果——不必要的拖延，这句因果就是答案句。 

 【替换】 This can create unnecessary delays ↔ It may prevent making a timely decision create delays=prevent a timely decision 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 本段反复念 achieve a consensus，A 项 It may cause lots of arguments in a team. 借"共识/团队"语境诱选，但原文讲的后果是"拖延"不是"争论"——求共识恰恰是为了避免分歧，说"引发大量争论"反而拧了。  借用原文：achieve a consensus 

 C) 偷换概念 It may give rise to a lot of unnecessary expenses. 顺着 you hold meetings 的开会画面联想到"花钱"，但原文 unnecessary 修饰的是 delays（拖延）不是 expenses（开销），是把"不必要的拖延"偷换成了"不必要的花费"。  借用原文：unnecessary delays 

 D) 过度推断 It may deprive a team of business opportunities. 说的"错失商业机会"在末段找不到对应，是从"拖延→可能误事"再往前推了一步的脑补，原文止于"拖延"。
